Legs.Subject: FixedQ1648.op_Multiply is pure in-process: two back-to-back calls on identical operands return identical bits. This observes hidden mutable state or an operand-independent result and nothing else, and is NOT the cross-run/cross-machine determinism contract
the declared bit-count constants (48/16/64), Radix, and the nine named constants (One, Epsilon, NegativeOne, Zero, MaxValue, MinValue, AdditiveIdentity, MultiplicativeIdentity, and the default value)

Legs.Subject: FixedQ1648.op_UnaryNegation, op_Increment and op_Decrement
Legs.Against: Oracles.WrapToRaw over the exact BigInteger −a, a + 2⁴⁸ and a − 2⁴⁸ — exact on both sides

Legs.Subject: unary plus is the identity at every swept raw, and negation is an involution over the full raw range including MinValue, where the two's-complement negation is its own fixed point
the increment and decrement operators are mutually inverse at every swept raw, and each equals the corresponding addition of One
all seven checked operators — addition, subtraction, unary negation, increment, decrement, multiplication and division — over every swept operand pair
Legs.Against: the exact BigInteger value of each operation, which decides BOTH halves of the statement: the operator must return that value when it lands inside [−2⁶³, 2⁶³ − 1] and must throw OverflowException when it does not. The multiplication's expected value is a locally derived Q1648ExactRoundedProduct and the division's Q1648ExactRoundedRatio, both routing through the SAME shared Oracles.RoundRationalTiesToEven body FixedQ4816's own ExactRoundedProduct/ExactRoundedRatio use, at shift 48 rather than their hardcoded 16, both UNWRAPPED, so the checked contract is decided by the exact rounded value rather than by the unchecked sibling

Legs.Subject: the seven checked operators agree BIT-FOR-BIT with their unchecked siblings on every operand pair whose exact value is representable — a wrapping operator and its checked twin differ only in the refusal, never in the answer

the two documented division refusals are distinct and both reachable: a zero divisor throws DivideByZeroException from BOTH the checked and the unchecked operator, and MinValue over NegativeOne throws OverflowException from the checked operator while the unchecked one wraps to MinValue

FixedQ1648.op_Division — the hardware 128-by-64 quotient under the raw_x >> 16 < raw_y gate, its UInt128 fallback, the r versus d − r tie test, and the magnitude-wrap-then-negate sign policy (structurally FixedQ4816.op_Division's shift-16-generalized sibling, at shift 48)

The widen-then-narrow round trip (TryFromFixedQ4816 then ToFixedQ4816) recovers the ORIGINAL FixedQ4816 value exactly at every raw where the widen succeeded, because the appended low bits are all zero and narrowing them back is the identity rather than a rounding event — this is the type's whole reason for existing, stated as a closed loop rather than as two one-directional checks
